reasons: Two specified manifest counters are not recorded, so the page cannot tell a partial run from a complete one.
Cost basis is not shown here, so the page does not cover the full provenance story.
The file has a test for the collapsed helper in views.test.ts, but no test covers the rendered page itself.

terms.meaning: a record written with each run that lists the exact versions of everything it used
a fingerprint of an agent's instructions, which changes whenever those instructions are edited
a fingerprint of the cached starting text sent to models, so a changed cache can be spotted
a saved copy of the reference material a run searched, so a replay can check it read the same data
a short fixed-length code computed from a longer value, used to detect changes
the level of evidence checking and critique a run paid for

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Page setup and imports
sections.what: Brings in the data type for the run manifest, the shared display pieces, and two number formatting helpers. The comment at the top says this page is the answer to why a result differs from last month's. It also says two counters are deliberately shown as absent, not as zero.
sections.why: The comment explains that the question is asked under pressure, so the page must be one click away. The page names the missing counters rather than showing a fake zero, because a zero nothing computed would mislead.
sections.watch_out: The attempted, completed and failed counters are not implemented, so this page cannot yet tell a partial run from a complete one.

sections.name: collapsed
sections.title: Reading a collapsed fingerprint
sections.what: Reads a fingerprint value that may combine several cached inputs into one string, such as a count followed by a digest. It splits the value into how many inputs were combined and the digest itself. A plain value is treated as a single input.
sections.why: The count is stored inside the string because the data schema has only one field for it. The comment says the reader should show the count so a multi-engagement run is not presented as a single one.
sections.watch_out: A value that does not match the expected pattern is treated as one input with no warning, so a malformed value would look like a normal single digest.

sections.name: Provenance (part 1)
sections.title: Run identity and version details
sections.what: Shows the run id, creation time, depth tier, engagement, classification, industry, trace reference and the versions of the manifest, record, taxonomy and ontology.
sections.why: The page note says a canonical id is only stable relative to its ontology version, so the versions are shown beside the identifiers.
sections.watch_out: The ontology version determines whether ids can be compared across runs, so compare it before comparing results.

sections.name: Provenance (part 2)
sections.title: Agents, models and prompts table
sections.what: Lists one row per agent with the exact model id and prompt version it used, and a summary line of agent count and distinct models.
sections.why: The section note says the exact model id is shown instead of a tier, because a tier is a routing choice and the id is what actually ran.
sections.watch_out: A prompt version changes only when the instructions or output shape are edited, not on each call.

sections.name: Provenance (part 3)
sections.title: Cache and retrieval corpus
sections.what: Shows the prefix hash and knowledge snapshot id. When several were combined, it shows how many and states that a changing prefix inside one engagement is a fault.
sections.why: Likely reason: these two fields let a reader see whether a re-run read the same cached text and the same corpus.
sections.watch_out: The count is carried inside the value and parsed out, so changing the value format breaks this display.

sections.name: Provenance (part 4)
sections.title: What this build cannot record
sections.what: Shows two warnings. One says the attempted, completed and failed counters are not recorded. The other says cost basis is held in the value engine instead of the manifest, and that rates are on the Portfolio view.
sections.why: The page says that a fake zero would be worse than the gap, so the gaps are named.
sections.watch_out: Do not treat the absence of counters as a clean run. The page cannot tell partial from complete.

summary: The manifest page that records what a run used, including its models, prompts, cache and retrieval snapshot, so that a change in results can be traced to a specific change.
purpose: Lets the owner answer why a figure moved since the last run, by showing which model, prompt version or data snapshot was used.
why: The file comment says the page exists for the question asked under pressure, and it refuses to show fields that were not recorded instead of showing zero.
how: First it reads the manifest and value output. It splits the cache and snapshot fields into a count and a digest where several runs were combined. Then it shows the run details, one row per agent with its exact model id and prompt version, the cache and corpus fields, a list of what this build cannot record, and the value engine's depth tier, duplication ratio, evidenced share and reconciliation basis.
inputs: The artifacts object, which carries the manifest and the value output.
outputs: A page of read-only tables, fields and warnings for a single run.
risks: Two counters the specification requires are not recorded, so a partial run looks the same as a complete one here. The page says so, but a reader could still miss the warning. Cost basis is also not on this page and sits in the value engine.
debug: If a field shows the wrong value, check the manifest that was loaded and the collapsed function, which parses the count from the digest string. If an agent is missing, check that the model ids and prompt versions cover the same agent names.
